why: my own caveat from this morning: both arms were measured 12-24 min after a flash, so 'settles with running' and 'accumulates until reset' were not separated. This removes the reset.

arms.arm: rested 47 min, no reflash, no reset

key_observation: the direction REVERSES when the reset is removed. With a flash before measuring, rested (37.5%) > hot (12.5%). Without one, rested (8.3%) < hot (25.0%). If rest were the variable both pairs would run the same way.
corrects: my own conclusion published on #48 this morning, that the drift is rest-reversible. The 'rested' arm was reflashed immediately before measuring and the 'hot' arm was 12 minutes past its flash, so the comparison had a reset difference inside it and I read it as a rest difference.
better_candidate: incidence decays with TIME SINCE RESET rather than with activity. Ordering the four arms by minutes since reset gives 0 -> 37.5%, 12 -> 12.5%, 15 -> 25.0%, 63 -> 8.3%, which is broadly decreasing and not clean. It also fits the two prior sessions on record: 'fresh' 41.7% and 'run-in' 8.3%.

statistics.note: neither pair is significant on its own. What carries information is the REVERSAL between the pairs, not either difference.

not_claimed: that time-since-reset is the mechanism - four arms and a non-monotonic ordering do not establish one
that the effect is thermal; nothing here measures temperature
that the morning result was noise - the reflash pair is real, it was just mis-attributed
